newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA re-opens talks on rules - paper.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA re-opens talks on rules - paper.

text.p: The Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) may be forced to drop part of a new proposal for disciplining senior executives of firms that run into serious financial trouble, The Independent newspaper reported on Thursday.

The SFA has agreed to re-open discussions over a shift in the burden of proof in disciplinary cases whereby executives would have to prove they acted correctly rather than the SFA having to show they failed in their duties, the newspaper said.
The proposed changes were drawn up by the SFA which regulates Britain's financial markets after the collapse of Barings Bank.

But according to The Independent legal advice sought by the Association of Private Client Investment Managers (APCIMS) suggests the move would violate the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights.
